title: Check and checkmate: the three ways out
outcomes: Gets out of check by moving the king, blocking, or capturing the checking piece
Says 'checkmate' when none of the three ways exists
Knows a knight's check cannot be blocked

steps.text: When your king is attacked it is in **check**. You must fix it at once, in one of three ways: **move** the king, **block** the attack with a piece, or **capture** the piece that gives check. You may never make a move that leaves your own king in check.

steps.caption: White is in check. The king can step away, the bishop can block, or the rook can capture.

steps.text: Not every way is always open. A **knight** attacks by jumping, so there is no line to block. If the king has no safe square, nothing can capture the checker and nothing can block, it is **checkmate**: the game ends and the player in check loses. Test all three ways before you say mate.

steps.caption: The rook checks along the back rank (the row where the pieces start). The king's own pawns take away three squares, the rook covers the other two, and nothing can block or capture. Checkmate.

steps.text: **When it holds.** Check is answered by a king move, a block or a capture, never by ignoring it. Blocking works only against a line (rook, bishop, queen) with a square between; a knight check or a pawn check cannot be blocked. A double check (two pieces giving check at once) cannot be fixed by one block or one capture, but you meet that later. *Rule of thumb:* list all three ways before you move; do not assume the king can step away, and do not assume a block exists.

steps.title: One pawn, opposite results
steps.prompt: Same rook check on the back rank. In one position the black pawn stands on f7; in the other it is missing. Predict first: which is checkmate? (The answer list also offers "stalemate", which a later lesson explains; neither position is one.)
In the last questions, which one did you answer by looking for the attacker first, and which by looking at the king's squares first? Rate how sure you were. (low / medium / high)
